title: Hybrid Stills for Craft Distilleries | Craft Beer School
desc: What a hybrid pot and column still is, what it can and cannot do for a craft distillery and the questions to ask before you buy one.
teaser: One still for whisky, gin and vodka sounds ideal. A hybrid can do it, with trade offs you should know before ordering.
standfirst: Hybrid stills combine a pot with a column of plates and often a gin basket. They are popular with craft distilleries that want to make several spirits on one site. This guide covers how they work and what to check before you spend the money.
sections:
A hybrid still is a pot still with a rectifying column bolted on top or alongside. The column holds a set of plates, often bubble cap plates, plus usually a dephlegmator, a small condenser at the top that sends some vapour back down as liquid. Many designs let the operator bypass the column or switch individual plates on and off.

With the plates off, the still behaves much like a pot still and gives a heavier, fuller spirit. With several plates in use, reflux rises and the spirit comes off stronger and lighter. With every plate on and the dephlegmator working hard, some hybrids can reach strengths in the low to mid 90s ABV in a single pass.

A new distillery may need to sell gin or vodka while its whisky matures for three years or more. A hybrid lets a small team make a whisky spirit one day and a vodka base or a gin the next, on one piece of kit with one set of utilities. That saves capital, floor space and installation work.

A hybrid can also do in one pass what a pot still does in two. Fewer runs mean less steam, less labour and less time per litre of pure alcohol. For a small site that is a real saving. Our guide to what a new distillery sells while whisky ages covers the commercial side.

Flexibility has costs. A hybrid is a compromise in each mode. It will not make spirit quite like a large classic pot still. It will not match a full multi column plant for a neutral spirit. A small hybrid making vodka base will usually need several runs or redistillation to get a truly neutral spirit.

Labelling rules matter too. Scotch single malt must be distilled in pot stills. Spirit from a column with active plates may not meet that definition. Other countries and Indian state rules have their own definitions, which can change. If you plan to call your whisky a single malt in any market, check the rules there before choosing a still design.
Sizing a hybrid for your plan

Start from the volume of spirit you want each year and work backwards. A rough sum: if you want 20,000 litres of pure alcohol a year and run 250 days, you need about 80 litres of pure alcohol a day. From an 8% wash, that is about 1,000 litres of wash a day, before any losses. Your pot needs to handle that in the number of runs a shift allows.

Leave headroom. Pots are usually charged to around two thirds of working capacity. Gin and whisky runs take different lengths of time. Our guide to sizing stills for a craft distillery goes through the sums in more detail.
Questions to ask a still maker

• How many plates are there? Can each one be bypassed on its own?
  • Is the pot heated by steam jacket, oil bath or direct electric elements? Steam gives the most even control.
  • How much copper is in the vapour path? Copper strips sulphur compounds. Stainless steel is cheaper but does not.
  • What is the maximum charge volume and at what fill level was the stated capacity measured?
  • Are electrics, sensors and pumps rated for a flammable atmosphere?
  • Who commissions the still, trains your team and supplies spares in India?

Get every answer in writing. Ask to see the still running at another site if you can. Taste spirit from it in each mode.

Hybrid stills need plenty of cooling water for the condenser and dephlegmator. In Indian summers, cooling water from a tower can run near 30 °C, which reduces condenser margin and makes reflux control harder. Size cooling for May, not for December. Factor in a water softening or treatment step so the condenser does not scale up.

The still room will also be a hazardous area for ethanol vapour, which affects the electrics and building layout. Your licensing adviser and a qualified safety engineer should see the layout before the still is ordered.

A hybrid makes sense when you need several spirits from a small site and accept some compromise in each. A classic pair of pot stills makes sense when single malt whisky is the whole plan. Write down the three spirits you most need to make in your first five years, then judge every quote against that list rather than against a brochure.
faqs: A pot still with a column of plates and usually a dephlegmator attached. The plates can often be switched on or off, so the still can make heavier pot still spirit or lighter, stronger spirit.
Can a hybrid still make single malt whisky?
It depends on the market's rules. Scotch single malt must be distilled in pot stills, so spirit made with active column plates may not qualify. Check the rules in each market you plan to sell in.
Can a hybrid still make vodka?
It can make a strong, light spirit, but a small hybrid usually needs more than one pass to reach a truly neutral spirit suitable for vodka.
Why does copper matter in a still?
Copper reacts with sulphur compounds in the vapour and removes many of them, giving a cleaner spirit.
